name: IM-1 Odysseus
operator: Intuitive Machines (US, commercial, flying NASA CLPS payloads)
short_status: Landed at 80.13°S near Malapert A on Feb 22, 2024; tipped ~30°, transmitted until Feb 29, 2024; did not survive lunar night (confirmed Mar 23, 2024).

facts.label: Organisations
facts.value: Intuitive Machines (US, commercial, flying NASA CLPS payloads)

facts.label: Launch
facts.value: 15 February 2024, 06:05 UTC (1:05 a.m. EST), SpaceX Falcon 9, LC-39A, Kennedy Space Center

facts.label: Landing site
facts.value: 80.13°S, 1.44°E, elevation 2,579 m, inside a degraded 1-km crater sloped 12°, near Malapert A; ~1.5 km from the intended site

facts.label: Firsts
facts.value: First commercial soft landing on the Moon; first US soft landing since Apollo 17 (December 1972); southernmost landing at the time

facts.label: NASA payloads
facts.value: 6 (NDL, LN-1, RFMG, ROLSES, SCALPSS, LRA) under a CLPS task order of about $118 million; all six returned data

facts.label: Rangefinder failure
facts.value: Laser rangefinders inoperable because a pre-launch safety-enable switch was never disarmed; discovered hours before descent; NDL patch uploaded during an extra lunar orbit

facts.label: The data flag
facts.value: Crain (28 Feb 2024): a missed validity flag meant NDL data 'did not process after all'; Odysseus landed on optical navigation and IMU only, with excess descent and lateral velocity

facts.label: Post-landing state
facts.value: At least one landing leg broken; lander tilted ~30° from vertical; downlink severely degraded but operational

facts.label: EagleCam
facts.value: Could not deploy during descent; ejected ~4 m from the lander 28 Feb 2024 but returned no images of Odysseus

facts.label: End of mission
facts.value: Powered down 29 February 2024 with a farewell image; wake-up listening from March 20; confirmed dead 23 March 2024

facts.label: What came next
facts.value: IM-2 Athena landed at 84.79°S on 6 March 2025 but tipped onto its side and ended within a day; IM-3 (Trinity, Reiner Gamma) targeted for early 2027 (as of October 2026)

timeline: Falcon 9 launch at 06:05 UTC from LC-39A, Kennedy Space Center
Laser rangefinders found dead hours before descent (safety switch never disarmed); extra orbit taken to patch in NASA's NDL payload
Touchdown at 23:23:53 UTC near Malapert A: first commercial Moon landing, first US soft landing in 51 years; weak signal confirmed ~15 minutes later
IM confirms the lander is tipped, resting at about 30 degrees; downlink limited
NASA's LRO photographs Odysseus on the surface at 18:57 UTC; LROC fixes the site at 80.13 S, 1.44 E
NASA and IM declare success (data from all six NASA payloads); Crain reveals the NDL data never processed; EagleCam ejected, no images
Odysseus sends a farewell image and is powered down ahead of lunar night
After listening since March 20, IM confirms Odie will not wake; mission permanently ends
Successor IM-2 Athena lands farther south (84.79 S, Mons Mouton) but tips onto its side; mission ends within a day
